paper.title_en: A genuinely non-Abelian plane-wave solution of the SU(2) Yang-Mills equations
paper.abstract_en: •Exact plane-wave solutions of SU(2) Yang-Mills equations: complete classification.•Genuinely non-Abelian waves require β × ℓ ≠ 0 and contain a nonlinear second harmonic.•Zero-action family links vacuum to non-Abelian waves; energy grows nonlinearly. We construct and classify exact complex plane-wave solutions of the vacuum SU(2) Yang–Mills equations using a simple ansatz for the gauge potentials. By reducing the nonlinear Yang–Mills equations to algebraic constraint conditions, we obtain a complete classification. For nonzero coupling and nonvanishing transverse and color-space parameters, the solutions can be reduced to a single fixed color generator by an SU(2) gauge transformation if and only if <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Therefore, the genuinely non-Abelian solutions are precisely those with <math altimg="si13.svg"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, occurring in subbranches of Cases (iii) and (vi). Their field strengths are of plane-wave type, satisfy the standard dispersion relation <math altimg="si14.svg"><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>, and contain a nonlinear second harmonic proportional to <math altimg="si15.svg"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo linebreak="badbreak">×</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>·</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>S</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mrow></math>. Although their quadratic Lorentz invariants vanish, the gauge-invariant Hermitian energy density can remain nonzero and exhibit a bounded modulation. We also show that a common amplitude rescaling generates an exact zero-action critical family connecting the vacuum to genuinely non-Abelian waves, with the phase-averaged Hermitian energy density growing nonlinearly with the amplitude. We further extend the solutions to arbitrary smooth wave profiles and construct a complex external current that generates a non-Abelian pulse from vacuum. Using this pulse as a background, we obtain an explicit relation between a probe gluon’s incoming and outgoing color amplitudes. These results provide a complete and transparent classification of Abelian-type and genuinely non-Abelian propagating waves in SU(2) Yang–Mills theory.
